transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. It's just this constant feeling that I’m a bad employee, and a bad homeowner, and... I keep thinking that I just deserve to lose everything I've worked for.
How long have you been feeling this way about yourself and your responsibilities? Has it been constant, or do you have periods where you feel better?

It's been pretty constant, actually. I don't really have times where I feel much better. Um... I'd say the depression and just... the loss of interest in everything have been with me for about two years and one month now.

During these past two years, have you ever had a period of several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt unusually confident or optimistic—even if it didn't feel as extreme as how bad you feel now?

No, not really. Um... I definitely haven't had any periods where I felt unusually energetic or confident. It's pretty much just been the exact opposite. I'm usually just exhausted, so... no, I haven't experienced anything like that.
Before this two-year period that started two years and one month ago, had you ever experienced a depressive episode or period of depression that lasted for several weeks or longer?

Um, no, I don't think so. Before this started a couple of years ago, I was doing pretty well. I mean, I had normal stress from work and everything, but... no, I never really felt depressed for weeks at a time before this. This is the first time I've ever dealt with something that just wouldn't go away.

You mentioned this has been going on for about two years and one month. During all that time, has there been any period—even just a week or two—where your mood lifted and you felt noticeably better, or has it truly been continuous without any breaks?

Well, looking back... it hasn't been completely without breaks, but close to it. The low mood and just... not caring about anything have been there for almost the whole time since this started. There were a few brief periods where I could function a little better and maybe get through the day slightly easier, but... they didn't last long at all. Mostly, it's just been continuous.
Over these past two years, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping more than usual, less than usual, or about the same as before this started?

I've been sleeping a lot less than usual. Most nights, I just lie awake for hours... I just kind of listen to the house settle. And then when I finally do fall asleep, I usually wake up around three or four in the morning. After that, I really can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work. It's just... really frustrating.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?

Yeah, my appetite has been kind of all over the place. But mostly, I just end up skipping real meals during the day. I don't really think about it, and then I'll notice that my clothes are fitting a lot looser than they used to. When I look back at what I've actually eaten, I realize I've basically just been living on coffee, maybe some toast... just whatever is the absolute easiest thing to grab.

During this time over the past two years, have you ever experienced beliefs that felt absolutely true to you—even if others disagreed—or have you ever heard voices or seen things that others around you couldn't perceive?

Yes... I have. Even during that one stretch I mentioned earlier, when my mood wasn't quite as heavy for a few weeks and I was getting through work a bit more normally... the other things didn't stop. I still heard this voice coming from near the air vents in my house. And I was... well, I'm still convinced that my coworkers and my mortgage company are monitoring me. It doesn't matter if I'm feeling totally down or a little better, those things just stay.

When you think back to when this all started two years ago, were you already hearing that voice from the air vents and believing that your coworkers and mortgage company were monitoring you right from the beginning? Or did those beliefs and the voice start later, after the depression and loss of interest had already begun?

They didn't start right at the very beginning. The... the depression and the loss of interest definitely came first. The voice and the feeling that I'm being watched started a little later. I'd say I've been dealing with those specific things for about a year and eight months now.

When you hear that voice from the air vents and feel that you're being monitored, do those experiences feel connected to your depressed mood and negative thoughts about yourself—like they're part of that depression—or do they feel like separate things that happen regardless of how your mood is doing?

They feel connected, I think. Like, they happen at the same time. During those same months when I was barely eating, not sleeping well, and just feeling like a complete failure, that's when I was also hearing the woman's voice from the vents. And that's when I was believing that people were watching me, waiting for me to make mistakes with my house and my job. So, yeah, they all seem to happen together.
